- Black king is on c8 (back rank)
- White has rook on d1, bishops on e6 and e2
- White pawn on a6 controls b7

**The best move is Rd8+**

This is a forcing check. The Black king's escape squares are severely limited:
- Kb7 is illegal (controlled by the a6 pawn)
- Kd7 is illegal (controlled by the rook on d8)
- Ka8, Kb8, or Kc7 are forced

After Kb8 (or Ka8), White plays Rd7, attacking a7 and dominating. If Kc7, White still has Rd7 with overwhelming pressure. This is essentially winning—the king is driven to the corner where it will be mated or lose material.

**Coaching Note:**
"Always scan for forcing moves, especially checks! Here, the Black king on c8 is trapped on the back rank. Rd8+ forces the king into the corner (Kb7 is blocked by your a6 pawn, Kd7 is controlled by your rook). After Rd7, Black's position collapses. Look for back-rank vulnerabilities."
